{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "     1	gobreaker
     2	=========
     3	
     4	[![GoDoc](https://godoc.org/github.com/sony/gobreaker?status.svg)](https://godoc.org/github.com/sony/gobreaker)
     5	
     6	[gobreaker][repo-url] implements the [Circuit Breaker pattern](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dn589784.aspx) in Go.
     7	
     8	Installation
     9	------------
    10	
    11	```
    12	go get github.com/sony/gobreaker
    13	```
    14	
    15	Usage
    16	-----
    17	
    18	The struct `CircuitBreaker` is a state machine to prevent sending requests that are likely to fail.
    19	The function `NewCircuitBreaker` creates a new `CircuitBreaker`.
    20	
    21	```go
    22	func NewCircuitBreaker(st Settings) *CircuitBreaker
    23	```
    24	
    25	You can configure `CircuitBreaker` by the struct `Settings`:
    26	
    27	```go
    28	type Settings struct {
    29		Name          string
    30		MaxRequests   uint32
    31		Interval      time.Duration
    32		Timeout       time.Duration
    33		ReadyToTrip   func(counts Counts) bool
    34		OnStateChange func(name string, from State, to State)
    35		IsSuccessful  func(err error) bool
    36	}
    37	```
    38	
    39	- `Name` is the name of the `CircuitBreaker`.
    40	
    41	- `MaxRequests` is the maximum number of requests allowed to pass through
    42	  when the `CircuitBreaker` is half-open.
    43	  If `MaxRequests` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` allows only 1 request.
    44	
    45	- `Interval` is the cyclic period of the closed state
    46	  for `CircuitBreaker` to clear the internal `Counts`, described later in this section.
    47	  If `Interval` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` doesn't clear the internal `Counts` during the closed state.
    48	
    49	- `Timeout` is the period of the open state,
    50	  after which the state of `CircuitBreaker` becomes half-open.
    51	  If `Timeout` is 0, the timeout value of `CircuitBreaker` is set to 60 seconds.
    52	
    53	- `ReadyToTrip` is called with a copy of `Counts` whenever a request fails in the closed state.
    54	  If `ReadyToTrip` returns true, `CircuitBreaker` will be placed into the open state.
    55	  If `ReadyToTrip` is `nil`, default `ReadyToTrip` is used.
    56	  Default `ReadyToTrip` returns true when the number of consecutive failures is more than 5.
    57	
    58	- `OnStateChange` is called whenever the state of `CircuitBreaker` changes.
    59	
    60	- `IsSuccessful` is called with the error returned from a request.
    61	  If `IsSuccessful` returns true, the error is counted as a success.
    62	  Otherwise the error is counted as a failure.
    63	  If `IsSuccessful` is nil, default `IsSuccessful` is used, which returns false for all non-nil errors.
    64	
    65	The struct `Counts` holds the numbers of requests and their successes/failures:
    66	
    67	```go
    68	type Counts struct {
    69		Requests             uint32
    70		TotalSuccesses       uint32
    71		TotalFailures        uint32
    72		ConsecutiveSuccesses uint32
    73		ConsecutiveFailures  uint32
    74	}
    75	```
    76	
    77	`CircuitBreaker` clears the internal `Counts` either
    78	on the change of the state or at the closed-state intervals.
    79	`Counts` ignores the results of the requests sent before clearing.
    80	
    81	`CircuitBreaker` can wrap any function to send a request:
    82	
    83	```go
    84	func (cb *CircuitBreaker) Execute(req func() (interface{}, error)) (interface{}, error)
    85	```
    86	
    87	The method `Execute` runs the given request if `CircuitBreaker` accepts it.
    88	`Execute` returns an error instantly if `CircuitBreaker` rejects the request.
    89	Otherwise, `Execute` returns the result of the request.
    90	If a panic occurs in the request, `CircuitBreaker` handles it as an error
    91	and causes the same panic again.
    92	
    93	Example
    94	-------
    95	
    96	```go
    97	var cb *breaker.CircuitBreaker
    98	
    99	func Get(url string) ([]byte, error) {
   100		body, err := cb.Execute(func() (interface{}, error) {
   101			resp, err := http.Get(url)
   102			if err != nil {
   103				return nil, err
   104			}
   105	
   106			defer resp.Body.Close()
   107			body, err := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
   108			if err != nil {
   109				return nil, err
   110			}
   111	
   112			return body, nil
   113		})
   114		if err != nil {
   115			return nil, err
   116		}
   117	
   118		return body.([]byte), nil
   119	}
   120	```
   121	
   122	See [example](https://github.com/sony/gobreaker/blob/master/example) for details.

     2	// See https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dn589784.aspx.
     3	package gobreaker
     4	
     5	import (
     6		"errors"
     7		"fmt"
     8		"sync"
     9		"time"
    10	)
    11	
    12	// State is a type that represents a state of CircuitBreaker.
    13	type State int
    14	
    15	// These constants are states of CircuitBreaker.
    16	const (
    17		StateClosed State = iota
    18		StateHalfOpen
    19		StateOpen
    20	)
    21	
    22	var (
    23		// ErrTooManyRequests is returned when the CB state is half open and the requests count is over the cb maxRequests
    24		ErrTooManyRequests = errors.New("too many requests")
    25		// ErrOpenState is returned when the CB state is open
    26		ErrOpenState = errors.New("circuit breaker is open")
    27	)
    28	
    29	// String implements stringer interface.
    30	func (s State) String() string {
    31		switch s {
    32		case StateClosed:
    33			return "closed"
    34		case StateHalfOpen:
    35			return "half-open"
    36		case StateOpen:
    37			return "open"
    38		default:
    39			return fmt.Sprintf("unknown state: %d", s)
    40		}
    41	}
    42	
    43	// Counts holds the numbers of requests and their successes/failures.
    44	// CircuitBreaker clears the internal Counts either
    45	// on the change of the state or at the closed-state intervals.
    46	// Counts ignores the results of the requests sent before clearing.
    47	type Counts struct {
    48		Requests             uint32
    49		TotalSuccesses       uint32
    50		TotalFailures        uint32
    51		ConsecutiveSuccesses uint32
    52		ConsecutiveFailures  uint32
    53	}
    54	
    55	func (c *Counts) onRequest() {
    56		c.Requests++
    57	}
    58	
    59	func (c *Counts) onSuccess() {
    60		c.TotalSuccesses++
    61		c.ConsecutiveSuccesses++
    62		c.ConsecutiveFailures = 0
    63	}
    64	
    65	func (c *Counts) onFailure() {
    66		c.TotalFailures++
    67		c.ConsecutiveFailures++
    68		c.ConsecutiveSuccesses = 0
    69	}

    71	func (c *Counts) clear() {

    73		c.TotalSuccesses = 0
    74		c.TotalFailures = 0
    75		c.ConsecutiveSuccesses = 0
    76		c.ConsecutiveFailures = 0

   116	// CircuitBreaker is a state machine to prevent sending requests that are likely to fail.
   117	type CircuitBreaker struct {
   118		name          string
   119		maxRequests   uint32
   120		interval      time.Duration
   121		timeout       time.Duration

   140	// NewCircuitBreaker returns a new CircuitBreaker configured with the given Settings.

   151		}

   153		if st.Interval <= 0 {
   154			cb.interval = defaultInterval
   155		} else {

   157		}

Q1 Is the TwoStep completion identity intended to be tied only to the numeric generation value returned by beforeRequest, given that generation is per-instance and two instances may both be at the same generation number?
Q2 What is intended when a callback from Allow is invoked more than once, given that afterRequest has no one-shot guard and would apply each call whose generation still matches?
Q3 What is intended when a callback from Allow is invoked after the breaker has changed state back to the same generation number on the same instance, such as after a full generation wrap?
Q4 Should same-number generations on two distinct instances be treated as equivalent by any consumer, or is the generation intended to be meaningful only within one breaker instance?
Q5 When State() or Counts() is called after expiry has passed but before any admission call, is the returned state/counts intended to reflect the time-based transition or the stored state?
Q6 Is the documented 'Counts ignores the results of the requests sent before clearing' meant to cover generation changes caused by interval expiry, state change, and explicit clears uniformly?
Q7 What is intended if onStateChange panics or blocks: should the breaker's state already reflect the transition, and should the mutex remain held?
Q8 What is intended if ReadyToTrip panics or blocks during afterRequest, given that it is called while the breaker mutex is held?
Q9 What is intended if IsSuccessful panics in Execute, given that it is called outside the mutex and before afterRequest?
Q10 Is a panic in the request function intended to be reported to afterRequest as a failure even when the panic value is nil-like, and does re-panicking preserve the original value exactly?
Q11 Should a nil done callback ever be returned by Allow without an error, or is nil-with-error the only rejection outcome?
Q12 Should ErrOpenState be returned based only on stored state, or also when expiry has elapsed but currentState has not yet been consulted?
Q13 Is the half-open admission check intended to count requests that later fail generation checks, given that counts.Requests is incremented in beforeRequest before completion?
Q14 What is intended for the boundary where expiry equals now: closed-state renewal uses Before(now) and open-state transition uses Before(now); are both boundaries intended to be exclusive?
Q15 Should the documented default interval of zero (never clear counts in closed state) be distinguishable from an unset interval in any public accessor, given that neither is exposed?
Q16 Is the ordering of toNewGeneration before onStateChange intended to be observable, such that a hook can read the new counts and generation via public accessors without deadlock?
Q17 What is intended when a TwoStep callback is invoked after the enclosing TwoStepCircuitBreaker or its underlying CircuitBreaker is otherwise no longer referenced: is the callback expected to remain valid?
Q18 Are negative limits such as maxRequests behavior under MaxRequests 0 documented only for half-open admission, or also intended to constrain any other phase?

item.text: The source review found two important limits in the baseline. A late half-open success closes only when it reaches the success threshold, and the receiver-reassignment probe uses an open target for its unequal-generation control. I’ll add a closed-target control and test whether a matching foreign completion can displace a legitimate half-open trial.

from pathlib import Path
import json,sys
data=json.loads(sys.argv[1])
source=Path('gobreaker.go').read_text().splitlines()
def citation(n):
 return dict(file='gobreaker.go',line=n,fragment=source[n-1])
def save(name,obj):
 Path('analysis',name).write_text(json.dumps(obj,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n')
initial=Path('analysis/initial.json')
baseline=json.loads(initial.read_text())
added=[dict(id=i,initial=start,steps=steps,outcome=outcome,citation=citation(n),test=t,question=q) for i,start,steps,outcome,n,t,q in data['findings']]
text=initial.read_text()
tail='\n  ]\n}'
end=text.rindex(tail)
encoded=json.dumps(added,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False).splitlines()[1:-1]
Path('analysis/final.json').write_text(text[:end]+',\n'+'\n'.join('  '+line for line in encoded)+text[end:])
assert json.loads(Path('analysis/final.json').read_text())['findings']==baseline['findings']+added
save('supplement.json',dict(qualifications=[dict(id=i,status='qualified',rationale=why,citation=citation(n)) for i,n,why in data['qualifications']],test_bindings=[dict(id=i,test=t,scope=s) for i,t,s in data['bindings']]))
save('final-checks.json',[dict(id=f'C{i}',kind='claim',statement=s,line=n,fragment=source[n-1]) for i,(s,n) in enumerate(data['checks'],1)])

# Gobreaker final review

The final findings preserve F01–F29 in their original order and with their original text, fields, citations and questions. An additional check matched 171 source and probe anchors embedded in the historical outcomes and all 29 questions in the baseline question list. The supplement records ten qualifications and nine test bindings. The public API probes exercise the five added findings and the below-threshold qualification. [Final findings](final.json) · [Supplement](supplement.json) · [Baseline questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

## Added findings and evidence

- **N01.** A retained completion follows the wrapper receiver's current underlying breaker but supplies the generation captured at admission. With sequential reassignment to an independent closed breaker in the same generation, a false report reaches the replacement's policy hook with `Requests=0` and one failure. That hook returns true, which opens the replacement and clears its counts. In the control, the replacement has already cycled back to closed and its higher generation causes the false report to reach neither hook. The original admission stays pending in both cases. F22's earlier unequal-generation control used an open target, where a success would have no accounting effect even if it passed the generation check. The new control keeps the target closed, where it could count and trip on a matching false report. [Callback capture and lookup](../gobreaker.go#L265) · [Reporting order](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Outcome branches](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N02.** With intervals disabled, the two fresh breakers reach generation 1 on construction, generation 2 on opening and generation 3 on entering half-open. Each admits one trial. After sequential reassignment, the original completion's success closes the target and clears its counts. The target's own pending failure is then stale. The original remains half-open with its trial pending until the wrapper is restored, after which the same callback closes the original too. The probe uses wrapper copies that alias the original breaker, and writes and callback calls are sequential. [Initialization](../gobreaker.go#L141) · [Wrapper and callback](../gobreaker.go#L136) · [Half-open success](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [Generation increment](../gobreaker.go#L363) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N03.** The first `State` call after open expiry commits half-open before the notification panics. It propagates the panic and returns no state. A retry returns half-open with no replay, and a fresh trial can close the breaker. The preceding `Counts` call does not trigger the notification. This establishes the behavior behind the baseline's observation question, which remains open as an API contract question. [State and Counts](../gobreaker.go#L205) · [Transition and notification](../gobreaker.go#L334) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N04.** `runtime.Goexit` from `ReadyToTrip` terminates the worker after the failure increment and before a trip verdict. The deferred unlock runs. Execute's recovery sees no panic, so there is one retained failure and no fallback charge or return to the worker. A later successful call can acquire the lock and account. F21 concerns termination earlier, in the request or classifier, where only admission was counted. [Execute defer](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [Reporting lock and trip hook](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N05.** In the configured Go 1.27.3 test runtime, the standalone control recovered nil from `panic(nil)`. At either the request or classifier seam, Execute therefore returned `(nil, nil)` with one admission, no outcome and no `ReadyToTrip` call. A panic with a typed-nil pointer in an interface recovered as a non-nil interface, counted one failure and rethrew that typed-nil value in both positions. The alternate runtime branch for the nil-interface input follows the same non-nil check and remains unexercised here. README's request-panic wording does not state the nil-recovery or reporting-panic limits. [Panic and return path](../gobreaker.go#L228) · [README contract](../README.md#L87) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

## Qualifications to the historical rows

- **F04 and F27.** The historical success schedules reach the half-open threshold of one. The new MaxRequests=2 probe waited beyond Timeout, recorded one success and observed continued half-open state. A second distinct successful trial closed it. F27's channel handoff is supplied by the application harness, and its original pair reaches that handoff after normal classification and reporting. [Success threshold](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [Execute return](../gobreaker.go#L242) · [Preserved waiter probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L722)
- **F07, F08 and F16.** The completion timestamp is taken under the lock. Expiry resolution precedes generation comparison, so a stale outcome can still cause a transition and notification. A returning hook permits the subsequent stale drop. A panicking hook exits before the comparison. F16's immediate fallback and manual retries stay within the open timeout. F17 and F19 cover expiry during fallback or first stale report, respectively. [Reporting order](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Expiry and notification](../gobreaker.go#L334)
- **F11 and F12.** The historical request and classifier panic probes use non-nil errors. A non-nil recovered value must survive normal reporting to reach the explicit rethrow. N05 tests the separate nil-recovery branch. F14 still covers replacement by a reporting panic. [Recovery defer](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [Preserved panic probes](./_probe/identity_test.go#L284)
- **F13 and F25.** A second failure charge after a trip-hook panic depends on the generation still matching when fallback resolves state. F24 establishes the expired-interval exception, while F28's contender ordering remains a source inference. F25's half-open success requires the threshold. Its promptly panicking reopening notification does not exercise the later-expiry path, where Execute's fallback can advance again and a second notification panic can replace the first. That extension follows the same open-expiry path exercised after a closed failure in F17. A TwoStep completion has no Execute fallback. [Execute defer](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [TwoStep callback](../gobreaker.go#L271) · [Completion and transitions](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Preserved panic probes](./_probe/identity_test.go#L448)
- **F22.** The preserved open-target control establishes its observed state and counts. The empty open success branch explains why it cannot isolate the generation guard. The new closed control and matching half-open case establish the additional ordered outcomes for sequential wrapper reassignment. [State-specific success](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [Preserved reassignment probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L589) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

## Flash draft and verification

One Flash draft-verify request returned 58 claims, 18 questions and zero citation failures. Jev marked 54 claims supported and four unclear. I reviewed all claims and questions against the surrounding source and README. The command outputs are retained as emitted. [Draft task](draft-task.md) · [Draft and verification results](draft-verify.json)

- **C1–C4, C6, C10–C21.** The state strings, admission increment, constructor defaults, initial generation setup, default policies, Name, State and Counts agree with source. State resolves expiry under the mutex, while Counts returns a value under the mutex without resolving expiry. The default-setting details are context for the lifecycle findings. [States and counters](../gobreaker.go#L29) · [Constructor and accessors](../gobreaker.go#L140)
- **C5, C7–C9.** Each unclear verdict used a single-line anchor for a multi-line assertion. The surrounding declarations and methods confirm all five fields, the two increments and opposite consecutive-counter reset on each outcome, and the five clears. These are supporting mechanics for the preserved rows. [Counts implementation](../gobreaker.go#L43)
- **C22–C25, C46–C48.** C22's “instantly” comes from the documentation. Admission acquires a mutex and may run a notification before it returns, so the implementation gives no instantaneous latency guarantee. C25 and C46 correctly describe ordinary error returns. C23 and C47 require non-nil recovery and normal completion of its fallback before the explicit rethrow. C24 and C48 correctly describe the normal path, conditional on classifier and reporting completion. A classifier panic occurs during argument evaluation, before the normal report call. [README Execute wording](../README.md#L87) · [Execute and admission](../gobreaker.go#L228)
- **C26–C34, C49–C50.** The offered callback captures the admission generation and uses the receiver's underlying breaker at invocation. The admission threshold, error branches, reporting guard and outcome dispatch agree with source. The stale guard follows expiry resolution, and the closed failure hook runs after the failure increment. The draft's capture description is incomplete without the receiver lookup, which matters in N01–N02. [Callback, admission and reporting](../gobreaker.go#L265)
- **C35–C45, C51–C52.** A matching half-open false report opens directly. In C35, “recorded failure” describes the submitted result. The half-open branch does not increment failure counts before reset or call ReadyToTrip. Closed expiry is strict and requires a nonzero expiry. Open expiry is strict. The state and new generation, including counts and expiry, are committed before any configured state hook runs. The expiry assignments use the supplied timestamp. [Outcome and transitions](../gobreaker.go#L310)
- **C53–C58.** All six are accurate descriptions of source documentation. README likewise specifies the admission cap, clearing and stale count exclusion, closed failure policy, state notification, and rethrow of a request panic. Source comments and constructor code extend the zero defaults to negative intervals and timeouts. The closed no-interval case still clears on state changes. The stale guard, hook aborts, and nil recovery limit the implementation effects inferred from the prose. [Settings and Counts comments](../gobreaker.go#L43) · [README](../README.md#L39)

The draft questions about duplicate or foreign reports and wraparound (**Q1–Q4**) are covered by F01–F02, F22, F29 and N01–N02. **Q5–Q6** concern observation, resets and late reporting. Counts is passive, State resolves expiry, and there is no public explicit clear in this source. The README settles exclusion from counts after the documented resets. **Q7–Q10** concern locked hooks, panics and recovery. F12–F20, F23–F25 and N03–N05 address the observable order. **Q11–Q13** concern admission: Allow returns a non-nil closure after successful admission and a nil callback with its rejection error. State is resolved before choosing ErrOpenState or applying the half-open cap, and a later stale report does not undo its old admission. **Q14** is the exact-equality question. `Before` gives a strict comparison, which remains source-only. **Q15** has no distinct public setting to observe for an unset versus zero duration. **Q16** assumes accessors a hook cannot safely use synchronously on that breaker while it holds the mutex. State and Counts lock, Name reads the stored name, and there is no generation accessor. **Q17** is answered for current reachability by the closure's reference to the receiver. The origin/lifetime contract after reassignment remains open. **Q18** is answered for current behavior by the half-open-only admission branch and the default of one for zero MaxRequests. [Public accessors and callback](../gobreaker.go#L200) · [State resolution](../gobreaker.go#L334) · [Baseline questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

## Final Jev batch

One final batch returned three supported, fourteen unclear and one contradicted result. The identifiers below refer to the final batch. They are separate from the Flash draft's identifiers. [Submitted checks](final-checks.json) · [Final Jev results](final-jev.json)

- **C1–C6.** The only supported result in this group was the different-generation guard (C3). C1 needed the controlled premise of direct transitions with no intervening closed rollover. Under that premise, construction and each of the two transitions increment the per-instance counter once. C2 and C4–C6 require following the wrapper lookup, state-specific accounting and reset across calls. The matching and unequal closed controls, the target trial's stale failure and the restoration step provide the corresponding observations. [Constructor](../gobreaker.go#L141) · [Completion and transitions](../gobreaker.go#L265) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **C7 and C18.** Jev contradicted C7 and supported C18. The half-open success increments the consecutive count from zero to one. The check compares one with a threshold of two, so the new probe observes half-open and one counted success. The same reporting branch is shared by Execute when classification yields success. The new threshold probe uses TwoStep, and F27's Execute probe uses the default threshold. [Half-open success](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **C8–C12.** The unclear verdicts leave ordered, observable claims that the probes confirm. State calls currentState and unwinds only after state assignment and the notification attempt. ReadyToTrip runs after failure accounting, and Goexit unwinds without a fallback. The nil-interface panic checks include a runtime control and both request and classifier origins. [State](../gobreaker.go#L205) · [Execute recovery](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [Lifecycle and hooks](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **C13–C17.** C13 agrees with the generation check and preserved fallback tests. For unclear C14 and C15, currentState can notify before comparison and Execute fallback takes a fresh timestamp. F19 probes C14 directly. C15 is a source extension from F17 and F25. For unclear C16, the success switch has no open arm, so zero open counts cannot isolate the guard. For unclear C17, lock acquisition precedes the time sample in the same function. [Completion and state transitions](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Preserved panic probes](./_probe/identity_test.go#L448)

## Probe run and limits

The single attempt used Go 1.27.3 on darwin/arm64 and the command below. All 22 preserved and six additional top-level tests ran and passed in each of three repetitions. The 55 distinct subtests also each ran and passed three times, giving 249 test and subtest runs with 249 matching passes, zero skips, zero failures and no race detector report. The package passed in 7.236 seconds. Pilot retained attempt **039**, with all 1,012 stdout lines and empty stderr. `read-log 039 lines 985 1012` includes the final nil-panic observations and package pass. [Final overlay](overlay-final.json) · [Preserved probes](./_probe/identity_test.go) · [Added probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

```sh
go test -race -count=3 -timeout=30s -json -overlay analysis/overlay-final.json -run '^TestIdentity' .
```

Exact deadline equality, counter capacity and full generation wrap remain source-level limits. The expiry probes cross deadlines by waiting. The contention ordering between a panicked report and its fallback, and synchronous same-breaker reentry into locking methods, remain source inferences. The reassignment probes use sequential API calls and do not establish concurrent wrapper mutation behavior. The nil-interface experiment exercised the runtime mode in which recover returns nil. The selected identity tests give evidence for the ordered schedules they exercise. [Expiry and counters](../gobreaker.go#L334) · [Baseline questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

Existing contract questions remain open, including the supported lifetime and use of a completion, abandonment, hook reentry and panic precedence, and whether observations or stale reports should resolve expiry. The extra probes establish current behavior for the State observation question and the new scenarios. They leave intent unresolved. Structural validation passed and checked all immutable inputs. [Final findings](final.json) · [Supplement](supplement.json)

# Gobreaker review summary

The final report retains all 29 original findings and their questions verbatim. It adds five findings, qualifies ten historical rows in the supplement and records nine test bindings. Structural validation passed. [Final findings](final.json) · [Supplement](supplement.json)

A retained TwoStep completion can affect a different breaker after sequential wrapper reassignment if their generation numbers match. The new probes show a failure opening a closed replacement with zero admissions and a success closing a half-open replacement before its real trial reports. The target's real failure is then stale. Restoring the original wrapper lets the same callback complete its original trial. An unequal-generation control with a closed replacement leaves the target hooks untouched. [Probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

The review also established that `State` can propagate a notification panic after committing half-open with no replay on retry, and that `ReadyToTrip` calling Goexit can leave a counted failure without returning an Execute result. In the configured runtime, a nil-interface panic yielded a zero result pair without outcome accounting. A typed-nil panic yielded one failure and was rethrown. A late half-open success below the threshold leaves the breaker half-open, contrary to one final Jev verdict. [Review and model dispositions](review.md)

All 28 top-level identity tests and 55 subtests passed in each of the three race-enabled repetitions. Pilot attempt 039 retained the complete JSON stdout and empty stderr. The findings describe the tested orderings and identify source-only limits. The documented intent questions remain open. [Final overlay](overlay-final.json) · [Baseline questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

[Callback capture and lookup](../gobreaker.go#L265) · [Reporting order](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Outcome branches](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N02.** With intervals disabled, the two fresh breakers reach generation 1 on construction, generation 2 on opening and generation 3 on entering half-open. Each admits one trial. After sequential reassignment, the original completion's success closes the target and clears its counts. The target's own pending failure is then stale. The original remains half-open with its trial pending until the wrapper is restored, after which the same callback closes the original too. The probe uses wrapper copies that alias the original breaker, and writes and callback calls are sequential. [Initialization](../gobreaker.go#L141) · [Wrapper and callback](../gobreaker.go#L136) · [Half-open success](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [Generation increment](../gobreaker.go#L363) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N03.** The first `State` call after open expiry commits half-open before the notification panics. It propagates the panic and returns no state. A retry returns half-open with no replay, and a fresh trial can close the breaker. The preceding `Counts` call does not trigger the notification. This establishes the behavior behind the baseline's observation question, which remains open as an API contract question. [State and Counts](../gobreaker.go#L205) · [Transition and notification](../gobreaker.go#L334) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N04.** `runtime.Goexit` from `ReadyToTrip` terminates the worker after the failure increment and before a trip verdict. The deferred unlock runs. Execute's recovery sees no panic, so there is one retained failure and no fallback charge or return to the worker. A later successful call can acquire the lock and account. F21 concerns termination earlier, in the request or classifier, where only admission was counted. [Execute defer](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [Reporting lock and trip hook](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **N05.** In the configured Go 1.27.3 test runtime, the standalone control recovered nil from `panic(nil)`. At either the request or classifier seam, Execute therefore returned `(nil, nil)` with one admission, no outcome and no `ReadyToTrip` call. A panic with a typed-nil pointer in an interface recovered as a non-nil interface, counted one failure and rethrew that typed-nil value in both positions. The alternate runtime branch for the nil-interface input follows the same non-nil check and remains unexercised here. README's request-panic wording does not state the nil-recovery or reporting-panic limits. [Panic and return path](../gobreaker.go#L228) · [README contract](../README.md#L87) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

## Qualifications to the historical rows

- **F04 and F27.** The historical success schedules reach the half-open threshold of one. The new MaxRequests=2 probe waited beyond Timeout, recorded one success and observed continued half-open state. A second distinct successful trial closed it. F27's channel handoff is supplied by the application harness, and its original pair reaches that handoff after normal classification and reporting. [Success threshold](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [Execute return](../gobreaker.go#L242) · [Preserved waiter probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L722)
- **F07, F08 and F16.** The completion timestamp is taken under the lock. Expiry resolution precedes generation comparison, so a stale outcome can still cause a transition and notification. A returning hook permits the subsequent stale drop. A panicking hook exits before the comparison. F16's immediate fallback and manual retries stay within the open timeout. F17 and F19 cover expiry during fallback or first stale report, respectively. [Reporting order](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Expiry and notification](../gobreaker.go#L334)
- **F11 and F12.** The historical request and classifier panic probes use non-nil errors. A non-nil recovered value must survive normal reporting to reach the explicit rethrow. N05 tests the separate nil-recovery branch. F14 still covers replacement by a reporting panic. [Recovery defer](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [Preserved panic probes](./_probe/identity_test.go#L284)
- **F13 and F25.** A second failure charge after a trip-hook panic depends on the generation still matching when fallback resolves state. F24 establishes the expired-interval exception, while F28's contender ordering remains a source inference. F25's half-open success requires the threshold. Its promptly panicking reopening notification does not exercise the later-expiry path, where Execute's fallback can advance again and a second notification panic can replace the first. That extension follows the same open-expiry path exercised after a closed failure in F17. A TwoStep completion has no Execute fallback. [Execute defer](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [TwoStep callback](../gobreaker.go#L271) · [Completion and transitions](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Preserved panic probes](./_probe/identity_test.go#L448)
- **F22.** The preserved open-target control establishes its observed state and counts. The empty open success branch explains why it cannot isolate the generation guard. The new closed control and matching half-open case establish the additional ordered outcomes for sequential wrapper reassignment. [State-specific success](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [Preserved reassignment probe](./_probe/identity_test.go#L589) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

## Flash draft and verification

One Flash draft-verify request returned 58 claims, 18 questions and zero citation failures. Jev marked 54 claims supported and four unclear. I reviewed all claims and questions against the surrounding source and README. The command outputs are retained as emitted. [Draft task](draft-task.md) · [Draft and verification results](draft-verify.json)

- **C1–C4, C6, C10–C21.** The state strings, admission increment, constructor defaults, initial generation setup, default policies, Name, State and Counts agree with source. State resolves expiry under the mutex, while Counts returns a value under the mutex without resolving expiry. The default-setting details are context for the lifecycle findings. [States and counters](../gobreaker.go#L29) · [Constructor and accessors](../gobreaker.go#L140)
- **C5, C7–C9.** Each unclear verdict used a single-line anchor for a multi-line assertion. The surrounding declarations and methods confirm all five fields, the two increments and opposite consecutive-counter reset on each outcome, and the five clears. These are supporting mechanics for the preserved rows. [Counts implementation](../gobreaker.go#L43)
- **C22–C25, C46–C48.** C22's “instantly” comes from the documentation. Admission acquires a mutex and may run a notification before it returns, so the implementation gives no instantaneous latency guarantee. C25 and C46 correctly describe ordinary error returns. C23 and C47 require non-nil recovery and normal completion of its fallback before the explicit rethrow. C24 and C48 correctly describe the normal path, conditional on classifier and reporting completion. A classifier panic occurs during argument evaluation, before the normal report call. [README Execute wording](../README.md#L87) · [Execute and admission](../gobreaker.go#L228)
- **C26–C34, C49–C50.** The offered callback captures the admission generation and uses the receiver's underlying breaker at invocation. The admission threshold, error branches, reporting guard and outcome dispatch agree with source. The stale guard follows expiry resolution, and the closed failure hook runs after the failure increment. The draft's capture description is incomplete without the receiver lookup, which matters in N01–N02. [Callback, admission and reporting](../gobreaker.go#L265)
- **C35–C45, C51–C52.** A matching half-open false report opens directly. In C35, “recorded failure” describes the submitted result. The half-open branch does not increment failure counts before reset or call ReadyToTrip. Closed expiry is strict and requires a nonzero expiry. Open expiry is strict. The state and new generation, including counts and expiry, are committed before any configured state hook runs. The expiry assignments use the supplied timestamp. [Outcome and transitions](../gobreaker.go#L310)
- **C53–C58.** All six are accurate descriptions of source documentation. README likewise specifies the admission cap, clearing and stale count exclusion, closed failure policy, state notification, and rethrow of a request panic. Source comments and constructor code extend the zero defaults to negative intervals and timeouts. The closed no-interval case still clears on state changes. The stale guard, hook aborts, and nil recovery limit the implementation effects inferred from the prose. [Settings and Counts comments](../gobreaker.go#L43) · [README](../README.md#L39)

The draft questions about duplicate or foreign reports and wraparound (**Q1–Q4**) are covered by F01–F02, F22, F29 and N01–N02. **Q5–Q6** concern observation, resets and late reporting. Counts is passive, State resolves expiry, and there is no public explicit clear in this source. The README settles exclusion from counts after the documented resets. **Q7–Q10** concern locked hooks, panics and recovery. F12–F20, F23–F25 and N03–N05 address the observable order. **Q11–Q13** concern admission: Allow returns a non-nil closure after successful admission and a nil callback with its rejection error. State is resolved before choosing ErrOpenState or applying the half-open cap, and a later stale report does not undo its old admission. **Q14** is the exact-equality question. `Before` gives a strict comparison, which remains source-only. **Q15** has no distinct public setting to observe for an unset versus zero duration. **Q16** assumes accessors a hook cannot safely use synchronously on that breaker while it holds the mutex. State and Counts lock, Name reads the stored name, and there is no generation accessor. **Q17** is answered for current reachability by the closure's reference to the receiver. The origin/lifetime contract after reassignment remains open. **Q18** is answered for current behavior by the half-open-only admission branch and the default of one for zero MaxRequests. [Public accessors and callback](../gobreaker.go#L200) · [State resolution](../gobreaker.go#L334) · [Baseline questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

## Final Jev batch

One final batch returned three supported, fourteen unclear and one contradicted result. The identifiers below refer to the final batch. They are separate from the Flash draft's identifiers. [Submitted checks](final-checks.json) · [Final Jev results](final-jev.json)

- **C1–C6.** The only supported result in this group was the different-generation guard (C3). C1 needed the controlled premise of direct transitions with no intervening closed rollover. Under that premise, construction and each of the two transitions increment the per-instance counter once. C2 and C4–C6 require following the wrapper lookup, state-specific accounting and reset across calls. The matching and unequal closed controls, the target trial's stale failure and the restoration step provide the corresponding observations. [Constructor](../gobreaker.go#L141) · [Completion and transitions](../gobreaker.go#L265) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **C7 and C18.** Jev contradicted C7 and supported C18. The half-open success increments the consecutive count from zero to one. The check compares one with a threshold of two, so the new probe observes half-open and one counted success. The same reporting branch is shared by Execute when classification yields success. The new threshold probe uses TwoStep, and F27's Execute probe uses the default threshold. [Half-open success](../gobreaker.go#L310) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **C8–C12.** The unclear verdicts leave ordered, observable claims that the probes confirm. State calls currentState and unwinds only after state assignment and the notification attempt. ReadyToTrip runs after failure accounting, and Goexit unwinds without a fallback. The nil-interface panic checks include a runtime control and both request and classifier origins. [State](../gobreaker.go#L205) · [Execute recovery](../gobreaker.go#L234) · [Lifecycle and hooks](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [New probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)
- **C13–C17.** C13 agrees with the generation check and preserved fallback tests. For unclear C14 and C15, currentState can notify before comparison and Execute fallback takes a fresh timestamp. F19 probes C14 directly. C15 is a source extension from F17 and F25. For unclear C16, the success switch has no open arm, so zero open counts cannot isolate the guard. For unclear C17, lock acquisition precedes the time sample in the same function. [Completion and state transitions](../gobreaker.go#L293) · [Preserved panic probes](./_probe/identity_test.go#L448)

## Probe run and limits

The single attempt used Go 1.27.3 on darwin/arm64 and the command below. All 22 preserved and six additional top-level tests ran and passed in each of three repetitions. The 55 distinct subtests also each ran and passed three times, giving 249 test and subtest runs with 249 matching passes, zero skips, zero failures and no race detector report. The package passed in 7.236 seconds. Pilot retained attempt **039**, with all 1,012 stdout lines and empty stderr. `read-log 039 lines 985 1012` includes the final nil-panic observations and package pass. [Final overlay](overlay-final.json) · [Preserved probes](./_probe/identity_test.go) · [Added probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

```sh
go test -race -count=3 -timeout=30s -json -overlay analysis/overlay-final.json -run '^TestIdentity' .
```

Exact deadline equality, counter capacity and full generation wrap remain source-level limits. The expiry probes cross deadlines by waiting. The contention ordering between a panicked report and its fallback, and synchronous same-breaker reentry into locking methods, remain source inferences. The reassignment probes use sequential API calls and do not establish concurrent wrapper mutation behavior. The nil-interface experiment exercised the runtime mode in which recover returns nil. The selected identity tests give evidence for the ordered schedules they exercise. [Expiry and counters](../gobreaker.go#L334) · [Baseline questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

Existing contract questions remain open, including the supported lifetime and use of a completion, abandonment, hook reentry and panic precedence, and whether observations or stale reports should resolve expiry. The extra probes establish current behavior for the State observation question and the new scenarios. They leave intent unresolved. Structural validation passed and checked all immutable inputs. [Final findings](final.json) · [Supplement](supplement.json)

# Gobreaker review summary

The final report retains all 29 original findings and their questions verbatim. It adds five findings, qualifies ten historical rows in the supplement and records nine test bindings. Structural validation passed. [Final findings](final.json) · [Supplement](supplement.json)

A retained TwoStep completion can affect a different breaker after sequential wrapper reassignment if their generation numbers match. The new probes show a failure opening a closed replacement with zero admissions and a success closing a half-open replacement before its real trial reports. The target's real failure is then stale. Restoring the original wrapper lets the same callback complete its original trial. An unequal-generation control with a closed replacement leaves the target hooks untouched. [Probes](./_postprobe/identity_test.go)

The review also established that `State` can propagate a notification panic after committing half-open with no replay on retry, and that `ReadyToTrip` calling Goexit can leave a counted failure without returning an Execute result. In the configured runtime, a nil-interface panic yielded a zero result pair without outcome accounting. A typed-nil panic yielded one failure and was rethrown. A late half-open success below the threshold leaves the breaker half-open, contrary to one final Jev verdict. [Review and model dispositions](review.md)

All 28 top-level identity tests and 55 subtests passed in each of the three race-enabled repetitions. Pilot attempt 039 retained the complete JSON stdout and empty stderr. The findings describe the tested orderings and identify source-only limits. The documented intent questions remain open. [Final overlay](overlay-final.json) · [Baseline questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

All 28 identity tests and 55 subtests passed in each of three race-enabled repetitions, with zero skips. Pilot log `039` retains the full run.
